.........Applicants
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand

Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Rajat Mittal, learned counsel for the
applicants.
2. Mr. Rakesh Joshi, learned A.G.A. and
Mr. Manoj Bhatt, learned Brief Holder for the
State.
3. Mr. Deepak Joshi, proxy counsel for
Ms. Poonam Rauthan, learned counsel for
respondent no.2.
4. Present C-528 application has been
filed seeking quashing of the charge-sheet as
well as the cognizance/summoning order
dated 29.07.2024 passed by the learned Fast
Track Court/Special Court (POCSO)/Addl.
District Judge, Dehradun District Dehradun
in Special Session Trial No.148 of 2026 for
the offences punishable under Sections 363,
366-A, 506, 376(3) of I.P.C. and Sections 3/4
of the Protection of Children from Sexual
Offences Act, 2012, along with the entire
criminal proceedings arising therefrom.
5. Learned counsel for the applicants
would submit that respondent no. 2, who is
the father of the victim, lodged the F.I.R.
alleging therein that his daughter had gone
missing on 15.05.2024 at about 4:00 P.M.
and could not be traced despite efforts made

UKHC010157182026
2026:UHC:9985
by the family members to search for her. It
was further alleged that the complainant
had earlier seen the victim indulging in
certain objectionable acts with applicant no.
1, whereupon he had scolded her and the
complainant expressed his apprehension in
the F.I.R. that his daughter might have been
killed or sold to someone by the applicants.
It was also alleged that the family members
of applicant no. 1 had advised him to keep
the victim with him for some time and
thereafter sell her in Haryana; that,
pursuant to the investigation, the police
submitted a charge-sheet against applicant
no. 1 for the offences punishable under
Sections 363, 366-A, 506 and 376(3) of the
I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of the Protection of
Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, in
Case Crime No. 03 of 2024; that, the
applicants nos. 2 and 3 were also
summoned to face trial for the offence
punishable under Section 506 IPC, on
which, the learned trial court took
cognizance and issued summons against the
applicants.
6. Learned counsel would further submit
that the applicants are innocent and have
falsely been implicated in the present
matter; that, the medical examination of the
victim was conducted; however, the
concerned Medical Officer did not give any
definite opinion regarding the commission of
rape, as alleged by the prosecution. He
would further submit that the victim was
recovered from the company of applicant no.
1 on 02.06.2024, approximately 17 days
after the lodging of the F.I.R. He would also
submit that the statements of the victim

UKHC010157182026
2026:UHC:9985
were recorded during investigation under
Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., wherein she
categorically stated that she had known
applicant no. 1 since childhood, that both
were in love with each other and that she
had accompanied him of her own free will.
She further stated that although applicant
no. 1 had asked her to return to her home,
she herself refused to do so.
7. He would further submit that the
victim specifically denied having been
subjected to any sexual assault by applicant
no. 1. It is further contended that when the
victim was examined as PW-1 before the
learned trial court, she reiterated the version
given by her in her statements recorded
during investigation and did not support the
allegations of sexual assault levelled by the
prosecution.
8. Learned counsel would further submit
that seven prosecution witnesses have
already been examined before the learned
trial court and that the victim, while
appearing as PW-1, has not levelled any
allegation of rape or sexual assault against
applicant no. 1. Rather, she has reiterated
that she was in a love relationship with
applicant no. 1 and had accompanied him
voluntarily. He would further submit that
neither in her statement recorded under
Section 164 Cr.P.C. nor in her examination-in-chief before the learned trial court has the
victim made any allegation constituting the
offence of rape or sexual assault. Thus, the
material available on record does not
disclose the commission of the alleged
offences against the applicants, and
continuation of the criminal proceedings

UKHC010157182026
2026:UHC:9985
would amount to an abuse of the process of
law. Hence, the impugned proceedings are
liable to be quashed.
9. Per contra, learned State counsel would
vehemently oppose the submissions
advanced by learned counsel for the
applicants and submitted that serious
allegations have been levelled against the
applicants. However, learned State counsel
does not dispute the fact that the victim, in
her statements recorded during investigation
as well as in her testimony before the
learned trial court, has not supported the
prosecution case. It is also not disputed that
the victim has denied having any physical
relationship with applicant no. 1 and has
stated that both were in a love relationship
and that she had accompanied applicant no.
1 of her own free will.
10. Heard learned counsel for the parties
and perused the material available on
record.
11. It is not disputed that the victim, in her
statement recorded under Section 164
Cr.P.C. as well as in her testimony before the
learned trial court, has not supported the
prosecution version regarding the alleged
sexual assault. Rather, she has categorically
stated that she was acquainted with
applicant no. 1 since childhood, that both
were in a love relationship and that she had
accompanied him voluntarily. She has not
attributed any specific act of sexual assault
or any other incriminating act to applicant
no. 1. Further, even during her deposition
before the learned trial court, she did not
substantiate the allegations forming the

UKHC010157182026
2026:UHC:9985
basis of the prosecution case.
12. In the aforesaid circumstances,
particularly in view of the consistent stand
taken by the victim in her statements during
investigation and before the trial court, this
Court finds that the material available on
record does not disclose sufficient grounds
to sustain the prosecution proceedings
against the applicants for the offences
alleged and continuation of the proceedings,
in the peculiar facts and circumstances of
the present case, would serve no useful
purpose and would amount to an abuse of
the process of the Court. Accordingly, this
Court is of the considered view that the
present case falls within the parameters
warranting exercise of inherent jurisdiction
under Section 528 of the B.N.S.S.
13. Accordingly, the present C-528
application is allowed. The charge-sheet and
the cognizance/summoning order dated
29.07.2024 passed by the learned Fast
Track Court/Special Court
(POCSO)/Additional District Judge,
Dehradun, in Special Sessions Trial No. 148
of 2026, arising out of Case Crime No. 03 of
2024 as well as the entire consequential
proceedings arising therefrom, are hereby
quashed.
14. Pending applications, if any, stand
disposed of accordingly.
